title: Life Agent device authentication wire contracts
description: Closed v1 contracts for one-time enrollment claim, fail-closed credential rotation and idempotent device-session revocation. Enrollment codes are created only by a local server CLI; there is no network admin endpoint. Malformed JSON, wrong body field types, or enrollment/refresh credentials outside their exact JSON-body lexical grammar are request_schema_invalid before lookup. Bearer Authorization is deliberately different: missing, duplicate, wrong scheme/spacing, or access-token text outside accessToken grammar returns neutral 401 credential_unavailable with fixed WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and performs no credential lookup; a well-formed unavailable access token returns the same wire response after keyed lookup. A neutral credential failure does not itself revoke a current family. Internal refresh-reuse revocation requires a retained exact successful-spend proof. Token-family tombstones and any replay HMAC key epochs they reference are retained for at least 30 days and at least as long as every live revoke replay record.

canonicalServerInstant.description: Canonical server instant in UTC only: uppercase T and Z, valid 24-hour hh:mm:ss, and either no fractional seconds or exactly three decimal digits. Calendar validity is additionally enforced by date-time format validation.

accessToken.description: laa_ followed by canonical unpadded base64url for exactly 32 server-generated random bytes. In bearer Authorization, missing/duplicate header, wrong scheme or spacing, or a value outside this grammar returns neutral 401 credential_unavailable with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and MUST NOT be looked up. A well-formed unknown, expired, revoked or superseded access token returns the same credential_unavailable after keyed lookup and MUST NOT revoke the current family. Access failure never invokes refresh-reuse detection. The server stores only HMAC(lookup_key, "access\u0000" || token); access and refresh domains and keys are distinct.

refreshToken.description: lar_ followed by canonical unpadded base64url for exactly 32 server-generated random bytes. A value outside this grammar is request_schema_invalid and MUST NOT be looked up. Every well-formed unavailable refresh token returns credential_unavailable externally. An unknown, expired, revoked or otherwise inactive token with no retained successful-spend proof MUST NOT revoke a current family. Only an exact lookup match to a retained record proving that this refresh token was spent by a successfully committed refresh is refresh reuse and atomically revokes that token's current family internally; the external response remains credential_unavailable. The server stores only HMAC(lookup_key, "refresh\u0000" || token); the access and refresh domains and keys MUST be distinct.

enrollmentCode.description: Exactly 28 uniformly sampled base32 symbols (140 bits) from a CSPRNG, grouped only for entry. A value outside this exact lexical grammar is request_schema_invalid and MUST NOT be looked up. Server policy for well-formed values: lookup HMAC only, TTL no more than 10 minutes, at most five failed attempts per code, and additional requester/global rate limits. After a code passes HMAC, TTL and attempt validation, it is atomically consumed before active-device and replacement-authorization policy is evaluated. Therefore active_device_exists or a disallowed replacement still consumes the validated code, and every retry requires a newly issued code. Well-formed unknown, expired, exhausted and already consumed codes receive the same enrollment_unavailable response.

access_expires_at.description: At most 15 minutes after this response server_time.

refresh_expires_at.description: At most 30 days after this response server_time and never after family_expires_at.

family_expires_at.description: Stable absolute family deadline, at most 90 days after initial enrollment. Rotation never extends it.

enrollmentClaimRequest.description: Processing order is lexical schema validation, code HMAC/TTL/attempt validation, atomic code consumption, then active-device and replacement policy. Once validation reaches atomic consumption, success, active_device_exists and disallowed replacement outcomes are all terminal for that code; retry requires a newly authorized code.

request_id.description: Correlation only. A lost successful response is not replayed and requires a newly authorized replacement enrollment.

replace_active_device.description: False can never evict an active device. True succeeds only when the code was issued with replacement permission. A code that passes HMAC/TTL/attempt validation is atomically consumed before this policy check: active_device_exists, replace_active_device=false against an active device, or replace_active_device=true without code authorization still consumes it. Retrying any such outcome requires a new code.

enrollmentClaimResponse.description: The server-person plus installation_id and local_owner_id maps to one stable device_id for the lifetime of that local identity. Re-enrollment of the known exact tuple reuses device_id and replaces or rotates only its credential family. A new device_id is issued only for a genuinely new installation/owner tuple under an authorized replacement. Reusing a known installation with another owner or a known owner with another installation fails closed as neutral enrollment_unavailable.

person_id.description: Opaque server-issued enrichment matching Android server_person_id. The backend derives the authenticated person from the token and never accepts a client-selected person or subject.

refreshRequest.description: The presented device_id, generation and refresh_token MUST exactly equal the active predecessor credential tuple already stored for this family. Every lexically well-formed unavailable tuple returns only credential_unavailable. Unknown, expired, revoked or inactive tuples without retained successful-spend proof do not revoke a current family. A tuple whose refresh token exactly matches a retained record proving successful prior refresh spend triggers internal family revocation as detected refresh reuse, while returning the same credential_unavailable. Success atomically marks the predecessor as successfully spent before issuing its exact successor; refresh is intentionally not replayable.

request_id.description: Correlation only. It does not make refresh idempotent.

generation.description: Generation of the presented active refresh credential. It must equal the stored predecessor generation used by refresh_token and device_id.

refresh_token.description: The exact refresh token from the active predecessor token pair; it is inseparable from the request device_id and generation.

refreshResponse.description: Success atomically records the presented refresh lookup hash as spent by this committed refresh and issues generation + 1 for the same device, with family_expires_at byte-equal to the predecessor value. The successor access_token and refresh_token are mutually distinct by token domain and each MUST differ from every access or refresh token previously issued in the family, not only from the presented refresh token. A later exact match to that retained successful-spend record revokes the current family internally as refresh reuse, while the external response remains credential_unavailable. Unknown or expired refresh tokens and old access tokens, including delayed requests, do not trigger that revocation. No successful refresh response is replayed.

revokeRequest.description: A new revocation attempt MUST present the latest active token-pair tuple. Replay lookup is scoped by endpoint, protocol, retained internal credential family, internal device and request_id. Only a resolved retained tombstone may replay after family inactivity. Exact retained raw-body fingerprint returns the frozen receipt before activity check; otherwise the credential is authenticated. Unknown well-formed credentials without a retained family/device tombstone return credential_unavailable and are never frozen. Only an active authenticated same-namespace request may produce request_id_collision for changed bytes, and collision/idempotency errors never overwrite or create a replay row.

request_id.description: Durable revoke replay identity within the authenticated replay namespace. An exact retained raw HTTP request BODY fingerprint returns the original frozen response BODY before current credential activity is considered.

generation.description: Generation of the latest issued refresh token pair presented by this request.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token from the latest issued token pair; it must match this request's device_id and generation.

revokeResponse.description: Revocation is durable and idempotent inside the resolved endpoint/protocol/internal-family/internal-device/request-id namespace. Exact retained raw HTTP BODY bytes return the byte-identical frozen response BODY even after revocation. A non-exact inactive credential returns credential_unavailable; request_id_collision is reachable only after active authentication and never overwrites the replay row. Revoke replay retention is at least max(token-family tombstone retention, 30 days); referenced replay-HMAC key epochs live at least as long. Android may keep revocation pending after timeout until a receipt or neutral credential_unavailable.
